principle is that reliability of a composite judgment system is governed by (1) bias of the component processors and (2) variance of their aggregation. An expert using intuition applies high-speed, low-effort Pattern Matching (System 1) that is vulnerable to the dual-process taxonomy's characteristic failure mode: substituting an available heuristic cue for the causatively relevant but effortful feature. The checklist forcibly shifts processing to deliberative, rule-based feature extraction (System 2), reducing systematic bias. The panel aggregates these independently extracted features; assuming stochastic independence of the non-experts' residual errors, the aggregation cancels unsystematic noise, driving the composite variance toward zero. The expert, operating alone, has no such variance-cancellation mechanism.
